CHIEF COMPLAINT
Pain in right middle finger

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
41-year-old female presents with four to five days of pain at the tip of her right middle finger following a motor vehicle accident. Patient was stopped at a four-way stop when she was rear-ended by another vehicle at low speed. The other driver appeared to be texting. While at the stop sign, patient became angry and attempted to gesture at the other driver but inadvertently struck the ceiling of her car with her right middle finger. This is her only injury from the accident. Car sustained minor trunk damage.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No other symptoms reported. Denies injuries elsewhere.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident as described above. Other driver appeared to be texting while driving.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right middle finger: Tenderness and pain with palpation over distal phalanx. No pain with palpation of more proximal aspects. Otherwise normal examination.

RESULTS
X-ray of right hand: Distal phalanx fracture of right middle finger

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of right middle finger
- Tramadol 50 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain; 8 tablets dispensed
- Finger splint applied
- Follow-up x-ray in 2 weeks
- Tramadol confirmed safe with concurrent digoxin therapy
